clue.text: I should take refuge off-shore, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: 'I should' contracts to I'D
IOM, the Isle of Man, is a famous offshore tax haven, a refuge for money

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to flee abroad, offered as a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: IOM is the usual abbreviation for the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea used as an offshore tax haven; 'take' just links I'D to it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a set expression, a characteristic way of putting things in a language.

clue.text: Noodles are often in difficulties

definitions.meaning: noodles are commonly served in a broth

explanation.surface: Noodles are frequently in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles float in broth, and the idiom means to be in serious trouble.

clue.text: Lump of metal —- nickel — thrown up and caught

indicators.note: in a down clue, thrown up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel
got means caught

explanation.surface: A lump of nickel is tossed in the air and caught.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, usually oblong.

clue.text: Silas dosed with a bit of iodised — salt

indicators.note: Marner is given a dose, so the letter goes inside his name

parts.note: Silas Marner, the weaver in George Eliot's novel

indicators.note: a bit of means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Silas takes salt mixed with a little iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like the iodised table kind but means an old sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an experienced sailor, a seaman.

clue.text: Assume permission to go on holiday

definitions.meaning: to have time off work, going away on leave

explanation.surface: Someone helps themselves to time off without asking.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to presume to do something and to take a spell of absence from duty.

clue.text: Start to turn and make firm stand

indicators.note: the start of the next word gives just its first letter

parts.note: to rivet is to fasten something firmly

explanation.surface: Begin to turn, then hold your ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivet is a three-legged stand for a pot or kettle.

clue.text: Part of computer vital to management of company

parts.note: key means crucial, as in a key player
the board of directors runs a company

explanation.surface: A computer component is crucial to running a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard is the set of keys used for typing input into a computer.

clue.text: Having learned swimming, he swam every night

indicators.note: swimming suggests letters moving about in a blur, rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who had learned to swim took a nightly dip.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend Leander swam the Hellespont every night to visit Hero, guided by her lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary youth of Abydos crossed the strait each night to reach his beloved.

clue.text: Port makes a move from one side to the other

parts.note: R is right, one side
a change is a move, as in a change of house
L is left, the other side

explanation.surface: A port switches from one side to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: Archangel is a Russian port on the White Sea. The R and L, right and left, are the two sides; A CHANGE sits between them in reading order A, R, CHANGE, L.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of Arkhangelsk is a major seaport in northern Russia.

clue.text: Delete the Times' editor's leader :

parts.note: times are periods or eras

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike out the newspaper editor's front-page editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times and its 'leader' (editorial) are the newspaper, but times here are eras.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to rub it out or wipe it.

clue.text: Indian princess making a bloomer

definitions.meaning: the Native American princess in J M Barrie's Peter Pan
a flowering plant, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A princess commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder or an item of underwear, but here it is simply a thing that blooms: a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrie gave the princess in Peter Pan this name, and it is also an orange spotted garden flower.

clue.text: African capital city, ranking among the leaders

definitions.text: African capital city, ranking among the leaders

indicators.note: the leaders are the first letters of the five words before this phrase

explanation.surface: A capital city in Africa ranks among the top ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Ghana is a large West African city on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Nation re-elected members to make an international agreement

indicators.note: the letters are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A country's newly re-elected parliament agrees a treaty with another state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' adds nothing to the letters: it belongs only to the surface, as the people voted back in.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1904 Anglo-French understanding is the classic example of a friendly pact between nations.

clue.text: Source of leather appropriate to fourth-rate shoe

parts.note: an ox provides hide for leather
'for' means suitable for, as in 'a job for him'
D is the fourth grade after A, B and C

explanation.surface: A poor-quality shoe should be made of ox-hide.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxford is a laced leather shoe, a standard style of men's footwear.

clue.text: To celebrate Hogmanay, drunken toffs riot

indicators.note: drunken suggests reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: At New Year, tipsy posh men run amok.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year's Eve; first-footing is being the first visitor across the threshold after midnight. Toffs are upper-class people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish custom is to be the first guest in a home after midnight on New Year, bearing gifts.

clue.text: Professional criminal to discontinue meetings

parts.note: PRO is short for professional
a rogue is a dishonest villain

explanation.surface: A career crook shuts down the gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: Prorogue is mainly a British parliamentary term: to suspend a session of Parliament without dissolving it.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue a legislature is to end its session so that its sittings stop for a time.

clue.text: When parting from oriental friend for ever…

indicators.note: parting from means the word for when leaves the word for oriental

parts.note: oriental means eastern
as means when, as in 'as I left'
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone separating from an Eastern friend, for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means always, without end.

clue.text: … reveal the end of the world is nigh

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
nigh means near or close

explanation.surface: Disclosing that doomsday approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to make known, to let out a secret.

clue.text: To get a likeness, left artist to it

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA is a Royal Academician
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wanting their picture painted leaves it to an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painted or drawn representation of a person.

clue.text: Spite voiced in private

indicators.note: voiced means said out loud, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, such as a private

explanation.surface: Malice expressed in confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in private' looks like secretly; 'in' is a link and the private is a common soldier, in non-rhotic speech sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, lasting resentment or ill will.

clue.text: School chasing king salmon

indicators.note: chasing means coming after the king in the answer

parts.note: GRI, Georgius Rex Imperator, King George as king and emperor, seen on old British coins
the LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A shoal of fish pursues a king salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' tempts as a shoal of fish beside 'salmon', and 'king salmon' as a species; but School is the LSE and the king is GRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A grilse is a young salmon returning from the sea to fresh water for the first time.

clue.text: I cause a reaction, making payment out of time

indicators.note: out of means the payment wraps around the outside of the time word

parts.note: rent is a regular payment
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A chemical speaks, having paid up beyond the deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance added to bring about a chemical reaction.

clue.text: Forge a common name —- and one unknown

parts.note: Smith is the commonest English surname
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Fake a common surname, plus one that is unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forge' looks like a verb, to fake, but is a noun: a blacksmith's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A smithy is a blacksmith's workshop.

clue.text: Abundant supply made accounting a complication

indicators.note: a complication tangles things, so the letters are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Bookkeeping made matters more difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a plentiful stock, like a joint of meat one can keep returning to.

clue.text: Better backing bird

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo
on means backing, as a bet placed on a horse

explanation.surface: A punter bets on a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' tempts as a gambler, with 'backing' as betting; but it is a verb, to cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table.

clue.text: Father divides pictures into pieces

indicators.note: divides means the father word splits the pictures word

parts.note: art means pictures or paintings
Pa is father

explanation.surface: Dad cuts up the paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn apart means broken to bits.

clue.text: Still around the house, go to the back

indicators.note: around means PTO is placed round the house abbreviation

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to go to the back of the page
HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Someone is still pottering about the home before heading out the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' is a noun: a single frame from a film, a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, especially one taken from a film.

clue.text: Where varnish may be found without delay

definitions.meaning: nail varnish is painted on a fingernail
promptly, especially of payment made at once

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the varnish is and wants it at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish sits on a fingernail, and paying this way means paying immediately.

clue.text: Bad reputation, one I try to shift

indicators.note: to shift is to move things about, so these letters change places

explanation.surface: Someone tries to escape their bad name.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, being widely known for misdeeds.

clue.text: Scruffy motor-cycle races across the river

indicators.note: across means the river spans the races, lying on both sides of them

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river
TT, the Tourist Trophy races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Bikers racing across a river look shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means worn and shabby, in poor condition.
